dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Field research across six comparable tools plus a same-day end-to-end express run identified five concrete friction points; learnings.md has never been created despite the plugin being its own heaviest user.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Five goals, each naming an observable artifact: routing question, generator-emitted contract.md, scoreboard line, summary confirmation, push-based learning capture.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Fifteen of sixteen criteria carry runnable checks (generator render + greps + engine tests); the routing/whimsy judgment call is named as such.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: User multi-selected all four jank items plus retro absorb+delete; express survives as pre-commit alias; exclusions (new agents, auto-saved learnings, critic changes) recorded with reasons.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The retro deletion propagates to every reference including both plugin manifests; the express/ideation section-reference coupling is dissolved by the thin-alias rewrite and verified by a no-step-citation check.

problem: The plugin's entry surface forces the ceremony decision before the information exists: users choose /ideation:ideation vs /ideation:express before the interview, yet the interview is identical in both and gate confidence plus criteria verifiability — the exact inputs for that choice — only exist after it. Six user-facing skills compound the surface-area problem.

The contract exists in three representations, one of them hand-authored: contract-data.json renders contract.html mechanically, but contract.md is hand-mirrored by the model, inviting drift, and the express skill needs ordering rules just to keep re-runs archiving cleanly. The plugin's own over-engineering critic flagged the unread third copy.

The interview gives no progress feedback — one-question-per-turn is correct elicitation, but the user cannot see how many gates remain, making interviews feel unbounded. The express confirmation has the opposite problem: a wall of terminal text (a 12-row criteria table plus tiers plus digest) duplicating what the rendered contract already shows.

The learning loop is structurally dead: /ideation:retro is pull-based (must be remembered at the moment of least motivation), empty-input-prone (clean runs produce nothing, training users it is pointless), and silently consumed (intake reads learnings.md invisibly). Field evidence is decisive — every adopted mechanism (Devin knowledge suggestions, Windsurf memories, Claude Code auto-memory) moved capture off the user, and Cursor removed its approval-gated Memories feature entirely. learnings.md has never been created in this repo.
goals: /ideation is the single default front door: identical interview, then a post-interview routing recommendation (express-style single confirmation vs full interactive review) derived from gate evidence and criteria verifiability; /ideation:express survives as a pre-commit alias that skips the routing question.

contract.md becomes generator output: contract-gen.ts renders it from contract-data.json alongside contract.html, preserving the exact structure autopilot's fallback parser and get-goal-prompt consume; neither skill hand-mirrors it again.
The interview shows a one-line gate scoreboard after each answer (e.g. 'Gates: 3/5 ready — open: criteria, scope'), inherited by both skills from the shared engine.
The express-style confirmation is a terminal summary (criteria counts, top checks, one line per critic lens) with full detail living in the rendered contract.

The learning loop goes push-based: interactive completions propose up to 3 candidate learnings with one accept/edit/dismiss question, intake visibly attributes any learning it applies and surfaces unmined implementation notes from prior unattended runs, and /ideation:retro is deleted with all references updated.

decisions.decision: Absorb retro into completion capture and intake attribution, then delete the command
decisions.rejected: Dropping the learning loop entirely, or keeping /ideation:retro as-is
decisions.reason: Field evidence shows pull-based retro ceremonies are never used (Cursor removed its equivalent; every adopted mechanism is push-based), but retro's generalization filter and dedupe/retire discipline are sound — only the trigger and visibility are broken.

decisions.decision: Keep /ideation:express as a pre-commit alias over the shared flow
decisions.rejected: Deleting the express command for a single-command surface
decisions.reason: Zero migration cost, preserves the ability to commit to walk-away mode upfront, and /ideation still becomes the default door.

decisions.decision: Move the ceremony choice to a post-interview routing recommendation
decisions.reason: Gate confidence and criteria verifiability are the routing inputs and they only exist after the interview; both skills already share the identical interview.

decisions.decision: contract.md becomes generator output from contract-data.json
decisions.rejected: Continuing to hand-mirror contract.md from the template
decisions.reason: Hand-mirroring is drift-prone (flagged by the plugin's own over-engineering critic); a generated md turns parser compatibility into a testable output contract.

decisions.decision: In the /ideation path the clean-tree check runs at routing time, not before the interview
decisions.rejected: Running the express Phase 0 tree check before every /ideation interview
decisions.reason: A clean tree is only needed if the user routes to immediate isolated execution, which is unknown pre-interview; the cost is one stash prompt after routing.

decisions.decision: Unattended runs never auto-capture learnings; the next interactive intake surfaces unmined notes
decisions.rejected: Auto-appending unreviewed learnings from headless completions
decisions.reason: Silent file writes erode trust and violate the accept/edit/dismiss contract; push-at-next-touch keeps capture human-approved without resurrecting a dead command.

decisions.decision: Express-style confirmation becomes a terminal summary with detail in the rendered contract
decisions.rejected: Keeping the full criteria table and digest inline in the terminal
decisions.reason: The 12-row wall duplicates the artifact the flow just rendered; the gate stays informed via counts, top checks, and one line per critic lens.

decisions.decision: Express alias is a thin pointer (~10-20 lines) into /ideation's routing path, which solely owns express semantics
decisions.rejected: Keeping express as a parallel skill file overriding ideation sections by reference
decisions.reason: Over-engineering critic: the parallel file's only remaining function post-routing is pre-answering one question, while its section-reference coupling taxes every future ideation edit — the same coupling that required hard constraints twice in one day.

decisions.decision: The generalization/dedupe/retire filter is written once in a shared reference and invoked at completion (bounded to the just-finished project) and intake (bounded unmined-notes scan)
decisions.rejected: Duplicating the filter logic inside execute-spec, autopilot, and the interview engine
decisions.reason: Three hot-path copies of mining logic would drift; one reference, two invocation points keeps the discipline testable and the intake scan cost bounded.

decisions.decision: Zero qualifying candidates at completion produces no prompt and no output
decisions.rejected: Always showing the capture question after interactive runs
decisions.reason: A mandatory prompt on clean runs recreates exactly the empty-input fatigue the problem statement condemns in retro.

decisions.decision: The retro-reference sweep includes both .claude-plugin manifest descriptions
decisions.rejected: Sweeping only skills/, references/, and README
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic blocker: plugin.json and marketplace.json both advertise /ideation:retro; without them in scope the plugin ships describing a command it no longer has while the check passes green.

decisions.decision: The full learnings.md lifecycle (bootstrap, entry format, dedupe amendments, retirement) relocates wholesale to the shared reference
decisions.rejected: Relocating only the generalization filter and leaving lifecycle rules to die with the retro command
decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic blocker: retro is the sole producer of learnings.md and intake is a format-dependent consumer; partial relocation lets the file rot with duplicates and stale entries — the exact decay retro existed to prevent.

decisions.decision: Generated contract.md keeps full parser-compatible structure as a deliberate legacy compatibility contract
decisions.rejected: A minimal human-readable md, since the fallback parser never fires for generator-produced projects (contract-data.json always exists)
decisions.reason: The structure is free at render time, keeps pre-JSON projects and the json-deleted recovery path working, and one smoke criterion is cheap; the live roles (locator, human record) get it for free.

decisions.decision: Lineage archiving treats generator-emitted html+md as a pair archived together
decisions.rejected: Keeping the sibling-md mtime heuristic unchanged
decisions.reason: The heuristic exists because hand-authored md was written after the html; when one invocation emits both, mtimes are near-equal and the comparison is meaningless — the archive step must handle the pair explicitly.

decisions.decision: The workflow example becomes a self-contained animated HTML page replacing references/workflow-example.md
decisions.rejected: Rewriting the markdown walkthrough in place
decisions.reason: User direction at contract approval: the walkthrough is human-facing and no skill instruction reads the md file, so the rendered treatment costs nothing downstream; resource lists must drop the dangling md reference.
